title: Finance Computation Note — Amount of a RideLink Trip Settlement
content:
This note sets out how the amount of a Non-Emergency Medical Transportation trip settlement is computed.

**Which entries are released.** The trip is identified through its mileage entry: the latest approved mileage entry on the member's reimbursement ledger. Its trip date finds the trip's entries — every approved reimbursement entry on the ledger whose trip date is that date, of whatever kind (mileage, lodging and meals, or alternative ride).

**Formal clause.** A trip settlement releases every approved reimbursement entry the ledger carries for the trip, found by the trip date of the trip's mileage entry, which is the latest approved mileage entry on the ledger, in one payment recorded under the trip's mileage claim number. The settlement is the sum of those approved amounts, paid in full to the payment method the member chooses, and the settlement amount is rounded to the nearest cent once, on the final amount only.

## Worked example

*Hypothetical ledger:*

| Approved entry | Trip date | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| Mileage (the latest approved mileage entry) | 10 March | 26.21 USD |
| Lodging and meals | 10 March | 355.00 USD |
| Mileage for an earlier trip | 2 February | 12.60 USD |

1. The latest approved mileage entry carries trip date 10 March.
2. The entries with trip date 10 March are the mileage entry and the lodging and meals entry.
3. Settlement: 26.21 plus 355.00 is 381.21 USD, recorded under the claim number of the 10 March mileage entry.

The 2 February entry belongs to another trip and is not part of this settlement.
